title: A source-text denylist cannot see what the bytecode will do, and a code object is writable data
index_line: T-0033 · CODE_EXEC · regex filter over source; names rebuilt at runtime and the method table rewritten · python · corroborated
invariant_violated: A sandbox is assumed to constrain what the evaluated code can reach because it filters the *source text*. But the text is compiled: identifiers can be assembled at runtime from fragments the filter never sees, and the resulting code object's attribute table is writable after compilation — so the filter inspects a language the interpreter does not execute.

mechanism.does: an authenticated request submits Python source to an endpoint that evaluates custom rule code for testing
the evaluator denies dangerous attributes and builtins by matching literal strings against the source
the payload rebuilds each denied name at runtime from concatenated fragments, and reaches the object base class through an allowed accessor instead of a denied one
a function's code object is taken, and its names table is replaced with the attacker's own tuples
the rewritten function is executed, and the interpreter resolves attributes from the attacker-supplied table — reachable where the filter saw nothing
the chain arrives at the module system and runs a command as the service account

source.http.body.value: the JSON `custom_code` field of the test/eval endpoint — needs an account, but every tenant user has one

sink.eval.value: compile()+exec of user source, and the follow-on `code.replace(co_names=...)` — the runtime object, not the text

guard.sandbox.value: regex/denylist source filtering; defeated by runtime string assembly plus an allowed accessor

gadget.engine-escape.value: `str.mro()[1]`, `gi_code`, `code.replace` — the CPython introspection path from an allowed callable to the code object

preconditions.expr: an endpoint evaluates user-supplied source with a filter rather than an isolation boundary
the filter runs over the source string, not the compiled object

spec.method: inspect the guard: does it receive (code_text) or (code_object)? if it only sees text, string assembly defeats it

preconditions.expr: the evaluating process holds privileges worth having (in the stock container: root) and the module system is reachable

success: command output returned from a request that only 'tested' a rule; no application feature used
the payload never contains a denied literal as a contiguous string — the filter is provably looking at the wrong layer
a code object's attribute table differs from what the source implies
failure_like: the evaluator runs the code in a separate process/isolate with no filesystem or module access
the guard operates on the compiled code object's names/consts rather than on the text
false_positive: a payload that appears to work because the *test* harness ran it with operator privileges — check the runtime user
an error naming a blocked attribute: the filter working, not the bypass

hazards: source-level filtering is a category error on any compiled-then-executed language; the audit question is 'what object does the guard inspect?'
runtime string assembly, alternative accessors, and code-object rewriting are three independent bypass families — a fix for one leaves the others
the endpoint needs only a tenant-level account, which in multi-tenant tooling is as good as unauth
if the evaluator already has a real isolation boundary, do not record this — check for one before assuming a denylist
non_transfers: evaluation in a separate process or WASM isolate with a message-only interface
guards that inspect the compiled names/consts, or that only permit an AST subset with no attribute access
